title: Lighting Circuit Test Sheet
source: spec/Lighting_Circuit_Test_Sheet.html — a project/location band, one circuit-by-circuit test table, a fixed five-function instrument table, a remarks box and a three-row sign-off. The supplied file was saved with the instrument make/model/serial/cert values filled in (Megger MIT310, Fluke 115, Megger RCDT310, Megger LTW315, Martindale CP501); those are record values — the kit changes as instruments are recalibrated or replaced — so only the function names are carried here. The source's own "Rev : 0 / Date" footer is not reproduced as a field: the printed footer already carries the template code and revision (SPEC §7), and a second revision on the same page invites the two to disagree.

sections.title: Circuit Test Results
sections._note:
`page_break_before` on the opening section is the grouping idiom: `paginate` gives every section its own page unless at least one declares a break, and a break on the first section is a no-op for layout — it is already page 1. Same as `fcu-lcp-checklist.json`.

**The paper's two-level header is flattened.** It spans "Insulation Resistance" across a P-N and a P-E sub-column; `dynamic_table` columns are flat, so the group name moves into each column's own label. Nothing is lost but the spanning cell.

**Insulation readings are `text`, not `number`.** A circuit that reads above the meter's range is written ">999", which a numeric column rejects — and on an insulation test that is the normal, passing result, so it is the one reading the sheet must never refuse. Volts is `number`: a voltage is always a figure.

**Unit conflict in the source, resolved to MΩ.** The column heads read "P-N (Ω)" and "P-E (Ω)" but the cells prompt "MΩ". Insulation resistance is measured in megohms and a reading in ohms would be four orders out, so the megohm prompt is taken as the correct one. Worth confirming against the paper master before Rev A hardens.

The source seeds nineteen blank rows; `min_rows` is five and the engineer adds what the board needs, so a record with six circuits prints six rows rather than six plus thirteen empty ones.

columns.label: Polarity
columns._note: The paper prompts a tick or a cross. Worded Pass / Fail here so the printed cell says what it means on a signed document, and so the outcome makes a failed polarity derivable as an outstanding item (SPEC §6).

sections.title: Test Instrument / Tools Required
sections._note:
**Why this section starts page 2.** Measured on the live build: a page gives 877px to content, a table row costs 35px. The circuit table alone runs to the full page once a board has any number of ways — nineteen circuits fills it — so the closing blocks go overleaf and page 1 belongs to the test results.

The five function names are the paper's fixed list and are seeded as template data; make, model, serial and certificate are the engineer's, and are not.

**Columns are the paper's four, which means no calibration DUE date.** This sheet records a certificate number, not an expiry. `link_to_instrument_register` is set for consistency with the other templates, but note it is a declarative flag today — nothing in the app reads it yet (record↔instrument linking is still to be built, see `lib/calibration.ts`). When it is built it will need a due date to judge expiry against, and this section would need a fifth column the paper does not have.

sections.title: Remarks
sections._note: A `field_group`, as on `condensate-pipe-flood-test.json`: a `standard` section always prints its serial and remarks columns, so a lone textarea row comes out as an empty serial column plus two columns both headed Remarks. The source is a plain box; this prints as one.

sections.title: Sign-off
sections._note:
An in-flow `sign_off` section rather than the top-level `footer`: PrintView always gives the footer a page of its own, which would add a third sheet carrying nothing but signatures. Both routes carry the same slots through `collectSignatureSlots`, so the status workflow is unchanged. Same idiom as `ductwork-air-leakage-test.json`.

The source's three rows, and it heads the lower two identically — "Witnessed By" — so the roles read the same here; the distinct `stage` values drive the workflow (SPEC §6).

The paper's sign block carries only Name, Signature and Date — no company. The renderer always prints Company, so Tested By defaults to Kenyon Pte Ltd and stays editable (unlocked, as on `staircase-pressurization.json`); the witness companies are left blank for whoever attends.
